newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds weaken as U.S. Treasuries skid.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds weaken as U.S. Treasuries skid.

text.p: Argentine bonds finished lower Wednesday in the wake of a plunge in U.S. Treasuries following Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's hawkish Humphrey-Hawkins testimony to Congress.
"The market was very long, but this is nothing to get worried about yet," said an analyst at a foreign bank. "I didn't really see clients selling."
Argentina's FRB due 2005 skidded 3/4 to 91-1/2 for a yield of 9.58 percent. The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 fell $0.35 to 126.60 to yield 8.52 percent.

Greenspan's statements that the Federal Reserve may have to raise official interest rates in anticipation of inflation "generated a correction in the market that was anticipated," said Hugo Diaz Lourenco, chief analyst at C&E Consultores.
The foreign bank analyst pointed out that the brunt of the declines were because "day traders were caught long."
Traders said this would not herald a turnaround in the still overwhelmingly strong mood in the Argentine market. A sharper rise in U.S. long bond yields would be necessary for that to happen.
Call money rates fell to 5.88 percent from 5.98 percent.
